_metadata.description: Health-guidance evidence: what health authorities say about intake, as opposed to what regulators have prohibited. This is the first evidence in the corpus that is not an enforcement action, and it exists because a risk scale that can only see enforcement reports "no restrictions found" for sugar and for trans fat alike. Three nutrients are covered: free sugars, sodium and saturated fat, plus trans fat's elimination target. Each is applied to the ingredients that are a major dietary source of it, which is a step of reasoning beyond what WHO wrote — WHO's guidelines are about nutrients, and a label names ingredients. The step is small and well established (salt is sodium; palm kernel oil is mostly saturated fat) but it is a step, and it is why the ingredients chosen are only the unambiguous ones. Oils that are NOT largely saturated — soybean, canola, sunflower, olive — deliberately carry no such record, and adding one to them would be wrong. REVIEW STATUS: ai_seeded. Sources, dates and determinations are real and named; the statements are accurate representations rather than verified verbatim extracts, and carry no URL — a guessed link is worse than none. Replacing these with verbatim text pulled from the published documents is a curation task, not a code change.

records.threshold: under 10% of total energy intake, ideally under 5%
records.statement: WHO recommends reducing the intake of free sugars to less than 10% of total energy intake, and suggests a further reduction to below 5%. Free sugars include sugars added to foods by the manufacturer, cook or consumer, plus sugars naturally present in honey, syrups and fruit juices.

records.threshold: elimination from the food supply
records.statement: WHO calls for the elimination of industrially-produced trans-fatty acids from the global food supply. Partially hydrogenated oils are their principal source. Trans-fat intake is associated with increased risk of coronary heart disease.

citation.title: REPLACE: An action package to eliminate industrially-produced trans-fatty acids

records.statement: FDA determined that partially hydrogenated oils are no longer Generally Recognized as Safe (GRAS) for any use in human food.

citation.title: Final Determination Regarding Partially Hydrogenated Oils

records.statement: JECFA has allocated Citric acid an ADI "not specified" — the designation used when a substance is of very low toxicity and its intake at the levels needed to achieve the desired technological effect does not represent a hazard to health.

records.threshold: under 5 g of salt a day, which is under 2 g of sodium
records.statement: WHO recommends that adults consume less than 2 g of sodium per day, equivalent to less than 5 g of salt, and that the recommendation be adjusted downward for children. High sodium intake raises blood pressure, which is a leading risk for heart disease and stroke; most people consume far more than the recommended amount, and the majority of it comes from processed food rather than the table.

citation.title: Guideline: Sodium intake for adults and children

records.threshold: saturated fat under 10% of total energy intake
records.statement: WHO recommends that adults and children limit saturated fatty acid intake to 10% of total energy intake, and replace it with polyunsaturated fat where possible, to reduce the risk of cardiovascular disease. Palm oil is roughly half saturated fat, which makes it one of the larger contributors in a typical diet.

citation.title: Saturated fatty acid and trans-fatty acid intake for adults and children: WHO guideline
